title: agentplane Agent manifest
description: The shape of an agentplane Agent manifest. The crate's parser stays authoritative: this schema refuses unknown fields, missing fields, and wrong types exactly as the parser does, but the parser's semantic refusals (an unstated budget, a declared control nothing performs) run only there — `agentplane validate` is the full check.

apiVersion.description: Which schema this document claims to be.

Metadata.description: Who this agent is, for the record.

version.description: Free-form, and compared only for equality. The crate does not parse semver: it has no version-ordering decision to make, and pretending to understand a scheme it never checks would invite one.

identity.description: Who the agent is told it is.

budgets.description: Absent means *unbounded*, and that is a decision the manifest has to state out loud — see `Manifest::validate`.

tools.description: Tools this agent may call. An empty list grants nothing.

context.description: External context this agent may retrieve.

oversight.description: Whether a human decides before this agent's answer is returned.

execution.description: How this agent runs — and whether it needs any code at all.

topology.description: What this agent is in a multi-agent arrangement.

models.description: Which models this agent runs on.

output.description: The shape of what this agent returns.

memory.description: What this agent reads from and writes to durable memory.

Identity.description: The words an agent is given about itself.

role.description: What the agent is for, in one line.

constraints.description: How it must behave. Kept separate from `role`(Self::role) because the two are reviewed by different people and change on different schedules.

max_sensitivity_egress.description: The highest sensitivity any value may reach an outward sink at. Combined with the sink's own ceiling at dispatch; the stricter limit wins.

max_sensitivity_journaled.description: The highest sensitivity a value may reach an effect **whose arguments the journal records**.

max_delegation_depth.description: How far authority may be re-delegated. Checked both against the runtime's configured identity and against every delegating sink before dispatch.

Sensitivity.description: How much damage disclosure would do.

Capabilities.description: What this agent offers, as capability strings.

Budgets.description: Ceilings, in the manifest's own vocabulary.

max_steps.description: Plan nodes this run may execute, checked before each one starts.

max_effects.description: Externally visible operations of **every** kind — a tool call, a clock read and a model completion each cost one, so this is not a model ceiling.

max_tokens.description: Metered units consumed, compared against the run's total before **every** effect — including effects that consume no tokens at all.

max_minor_units.description: Money in minor units — cents, not euros. A float here would make a budget that fails to bind by a rounding error, and money is the one number nobody accepts "approximately" for.

max_replans.description: How many times the run may change its plan.

max_wallclock_secs.description: Seconds. Named for its unit so a manifest cannot mean minutes.

ToolGrant.description: One tool this agent may call, and on what terms.

mutates.description: Whether calling it changes the world.

max_sensitivity.description: The highest sensitivity this tool may be shown.

protected_fields.description: Authority-bearing JSON arguments and the lineage each is allowed to derive from. These rules are part of the canonical manifest digest.

description.description: What this tool does, in the words the **model** is given.

requires_approval.description: Whether a person approves each call, before it happens.

arguments.description: A JSON Schema for the arguments, carried opaquely.

ProtectedField.description: A stricter information-flow rule for one JSON field sent to a sink.

one_of.description: The closed set of values this field may carry, when one is declared.

SourceId.description: Where a value came from. Free-form so the engine stays domain-agnostic; the runtime stamps tool refs, peer ids, and collection names.

task_input.description: Servers this agent may answer `tasks/update` input requests on.

ContextTaskInput.description: One server this agent may send task input responses to.

Oversight.description: Human oversight, declared rather than remembered.

approval.description: What a human decides **before** the run continues.

approvers.description: Who may decide. Empty means anyone — a choice worth making on purpose rather than by omission.

deadline.description: The obligation that bounds the wait.

on_expiry.description: What happens when the window closes.

escalate_to.description: Who is added to the audience when an unanswered task escalates.

allow_unattended.description: Explicit consent to act with no human when the window closes.

triage.description: Tasks opened **beside** a completed answer, not in front of it.

Approval.description: What a human decides on **before the run continues**.

oneOf.description: Every answer waits for a person.
Only the tool calls that ask for it wait; the answer returns unattended.
Nothing waits. The run completes and `Oversight::triage` decides what a person is shown afterwards.

OversightDeadline.description: The obligation that bounds an oversight wait.

name.description: What the obligation is called on the case.

params.description: Parameters for that rule, e.g. `{ n: 2 }`.

Expiry.description: What happens when the approval window closes.

oneOf.description: Refuse the answer. The safe default, and the default here.
Widen the audience and keep waiting.
Return the answer with nobody having looked.

TriageRule.description: One reason to put an answer in front of a person, and who.

name.description: What the task is called, so a worklist can be filtered on it.

when.description: Every condition that must hold. Conjunctive, and an empty list is refused — a rule matching everything is a task per run written as a filter.

audience.description: Roles that may act on the task. Empty means anyone, which is a choice worth making on purpose rather than by omission.

summary.description: What the worklist row says, in the words a reviewer reads.

deadline.description: The obligation that bounds the task.

Condition.description: One field of the answer, and one thing that must be true of it.

path.description: RFC 6901 pointer into the answer, e.g. `/deadline_status`.

oneOf.description: Deep JSON equality against a constant.
Deep JSON equality against any of several constants.
A number at or above this. Non-numbers do not match.
A number at or below this. Non-numbers do not match.
The pointer selects something — anything, including `null`.

TriagePriority.description: How a triage task is ranked in a worklist.

kind.description: Which built-in behaviour runs this agent.

max_turns.description: How many model turns a tool-calling agent may take.

ExecutionKind.description: The built-in behaviours a manifest may ask for.

oneOf.description: One model call, answered in the declared `Output` shape.
Call tools until the model stops asking, then answer.
Plan first over trusted input, then execute without the model.

Topology.description: Where this agent sits in a multi-agent arrangement.

mode.description: How many agents, and therefore how much coordination risk.

role.description: What this agent is within that shape.

TopologyMode.description: How many agents contribute to one task.

oneOf.description: One agent, one context, many tools. Inter-agent failure is structurally absent, which is why it is the default.
Several agents contribute to one task. The full failure surface.

Role.description: What an agent is within an arrangement.

oneOf.description: Does one thing and hands off to nobody.
Decomposes a task, delegates to specialists, assembles the result.

Justification.description: Why collaboration is worth its cost.

oneOf.description: Sub-tasks operate on provably disjoint inputs.
Sub-tasks require strictly different capabilities.

Models.description: The models an agent runs on, by role.

privileged.description: The model trusted with tool calls and decisions.

quarantined.description: The model that reads untrusted material and holds no authority.

ModelRef.description: One model, named the way a provider names it.

provider.description: The driver: `anthropic`, `openai`, or whatever an embedder registered.

model.description: The provider's own model identifier, pinned exactly.

max_tokens.description: A per-call output ceiling, if this role needs one.

reasoning_effort.description: Explicit reasoning depth. Omitted uses the selected model's default.

Output.description: The shape an agent promises its callers.

Memory.description: A declarative agent's two halves of durable memory: what it reads, and what it writes.

recall.description: Read memories into the prompt, before the model is called.

formation.description: Form bounded durable facts from each answer.

MemoryRecall.description: What a declarative agent is given to remember, before it answers.

subject.description: Which pile to read, with the same three bindings formation writes under. See `MemorySubject`.

purpose.description: Restrict to memories kept for one purpose.

refresh_access.description: Slide each selected memory's access-retention window forward.

MemorySubject.description: A memory scope: a literal name, or a run binding — `$correlation/<namespace>`, `$case`, or `$input/<RFC 6901 pointer>`. Write `$$` for a literal that really begins with a dollar sign; any other `$` spelling is refused rather than read as a constant.

subject.description: Where the formed memories are filed.
